Daily Devotional

February 4

27 And hath given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of man. 28 Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, 29 And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation. (John 5:27-29 KJV)

When Jesus referred to Himself as the Son of man, He is referring to the fact that He was physical, and had a human body (John 1:14). When He said Son of God, He was referring to His divinity, as He was God in the flesh (John 14:10). This gave Jesus authority on earth and in heaven (Matthew 28:18). Notice that Jesus is saying that all that have died would hear His voice and be resurrected, not only the saved ones, but also all that have died. This shows us that we all will live forever, not just the saints, and we need to be aware that when we die we do not cease to exist, as our soul is a spiritual being, and will never die.

When Jesus comes again and all the saints are resurrected back to life, which is the first resurrection (Revelation 20:6), we will appear before Jesus to give an account of our actions. The ones that have died as unbelievers in Jesus will appear before God, after the thousand year reign of Jesus, which is the second resurrection (Revelation 20:5). They will be judged by God at the Great White Throne Judgement, then the unbelievers will be cast into the lake of fire, which is the second death, but they will then live forever in torment along with the devil and his demons (Revelation 20:15). Boy, I think I would rather be with Jesus, and live forever in the New Jerusalem on the new earth (Revelation 21:2), where God will live with us for eternity (Revelation 21:3), and there will be no more death, sorrow, or pain (Revelation 21:4). For a complete timeline of the end times, see our web page “New Revelations”. Thank you Jesus for my salvation.
